contributions: Introduces GEA, a paradigm treating a group of agents as the fundamental evolutionary unit with explicit experience sharing and reuse
Overcomes the limitation of inefficient utilization of exploratory diversity caused by isolated evolutionary branches in tree-structured evolution
Demonstrates consistent transferability across different coding models and stronger robustness to framework-level perturbations
limitations: The paper does not explicitly state limitations. Computational budget constraints are noted as a practical consideration driving the staged evaluation strategy and the use of different model sizes across iterations.
methods: GEA selects a parent group using a Performance-Novelty criterion balancing task performance and evolutionary diversity based on cosine distance over task-success vectors. Each selected agent contributes evolutionary traces (code patches, predicted task patches, execution logs, and outcome logs) to a shared pool. A reflection module analyzes shared experience to produce evolution directives, an evolution module generates framework-level patches, and an acting module evaluates updated agents on downstream programming tasks. Agents that compile and exhibit basic coding functionality are retained in the archive.
results: GEA achieves 71.0% on SWE-bench Verified (vs. 56.7% for the DGM self-evolving baseline) and 88.3% on Polyglot (vs. 68.3% for the baseline). It matches or exceeds top human-designed frameworks: 71.0% vs. 71.8% on SWE-bench Verified and 88.3% vs. 52.0% on Polyglot. GEA fixes framework-level bugs in 1.4 iterations on average, versus 5 for self-evolving methods. On Polyglot, GEA reaches 88.3% in 4 iterations with 8,677 lines of code added; on SWE-bench Verified it reaches 71.0% in 8 iterations with 9,663 lines added.
tldr: Group-Evolving Agents (GEA) introduces a group-centric open-ended self-improvement paradigm that enables explicit experience sharing and reuse across agents, significantly outperforming tree-structured self-evolving methods on coding benchmarks.
